name: Ice
height_note: H 0..65535 spans height_range_m; mid level about 0.000

colour_spaces.N: linear, OpenGL (+Y up); flip green on Unreal import
colour_spaces.ORM: linear; R AO, G roughness, B metallic 0
colour_spaces.Macro: linear; R large, G medium, B small low-frequency variation, sample at 1/6 to 1/10 of the tile UV scale

method: lake ice built here (no CC0 ice scan is in the project): a dark clear body with cloudy air-rich ice, bubble clouds, eleven long branching fracture sheets with a milky plane beside each and many hairline cracks, and thin wind-streaked wisps of blown snow and hoar (fine normal from ambientCG Snow008A). H is the depth at which each thing lies inside the sheet (0 = body 7 cm down, 1 = surface), for the parallax march of the Unreal material; the normal map is the nearly flat surface
known_weaknesses: fractures are drawn random walks, not a scan: no pressure ridges, no refrozen leads; no real refraction or translucency (the depth is parallax only); frost patches are noise shaped
